transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Rivera (Beta Analytics Head of ML), Mark Chen (Platform Eng), Priya Desai (PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping for Beta Analytics POC focused on defining latency / throughput SLOs and measurement plan. Discussed TTFT (time to first token) vs TPOT (time per token), p95/p99 targets, workload sizing (qps, concurrency, prompt lengths), and an execution timeline for a 2-3 week benchmark-led POC. Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Success criteria and stakeholders
- Definitions: TTFT vs TPOT, measurement semantics
- SLO targets: p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT, tail behavior
- Workload sizing: concurrency, QPS, prompt and generation length distro
- Benchmark plan: warm vs cold cache, steady-state vs burst tests, tooling
- Timeline & next steps for POC

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, I'm Ava, I'm the AE for the account, and with me is Samir our SE.
[00:12] Samir: hey all, Samir here, I'll drive the benchmark plan and the test harness.
[00:18] Lena: hi Ava, Samir, thanks. I'm lena, head of ML here. Mark and Priya are on from infra and product.
[00:27] Mark: hi.
[00:29] Priya: hey.
[00:31] Ava: cool. objective today is to align on what success looks like for the POC - specifically latency and throughput SLOs and how we measure them. we also want to size the workload so our benchmark is representative.
[00:44] Priya: quick context - our main user flow is a 1) short question -> 2) 80-150 token responses used in product search-ranking and rewriting. target concurrent users ~200, but backend concurrency peaks at around 60 requests/sec during spikes.
[00:59] Mark: infra note - we care about p99 tail because spikes correlate to user-visible timeouts; we also have a strict 250ms budget for first token in the search path if we can't meet it we need fallback to cached answer.
[01:12] Samir: ok good, that gives us clear constraints. so two important metrics we typically scope: TTFT (time to first token) - that is from request arrival to the first output token, and TPOT (time per output token / per-token throughput) which matters for longer generations. we measure both p95 and p99 for each.
[01:31] Lena: can you clarify difference in measurement? sometimes our product teams conflate average latency with tail.
[01:35] Samir: sure. TTFT is sensitive to model startup, KV cache warmness, and routing. TPOT is more steady-state - it reflects token generation speed once streaming begins. for SLOs you often specify both, e.g., TTFT p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms for short queries; TPOT p95 < 25ms/token, p99 < 60ms/token for longer responses. those numbers are examples and we'll calibrate to your model.
[01:58] Ava: lena, mark — are those example thresholds in the ballpark or do you have stricter internal SLAs?
[02:05] Lena: first token <250ms p95 would be acceptable, but p99 we'd prefer under 500ms. TPOT we can tolerate up to 50ms p95 for our 100-token generations but p99 should be under 150ms ideally.
[02:18] Mark: to add, any solution must degrade gracefully. if a dedicated offering can't meet p99 we need automatic fallback to a cheaper endpoint or cached responses within 300ms.
[02:28] Samir: that's reasonable. we'll design the POC to measure both dedicated and hosted variants and include fallback verification.
[02:35] Priya: what about throughput? during batch processing we also hit sustained 100 qps over 10 minutes and occasional bursts to 200 qps for 30s.
[02:44] Samir: ok. so test matrix will include steady-state 100 qps, short 30s bursts to 200 qps, and spike tests. also concurrent users 60 concurrent requests with mix of short (<=32 tokens) and medium (80-150 tokens) prompts. we should collect token distributions.
[03:02] Lena: do you need sample traffic traces? we can provide 72h traces from staging.
[03:07] Ava: yes please, that will help us replay realistic payload sizes and client-side pacing. Mark, can you export?
[03:12] Mark: yes I'll export and sanitize PII.
[03:15] Samir: measurement specifics: we'll record TTFT and per-token timings at the request level and compute service-side p50/p95/p99; we'll also measure end-to-end from client to first byte to catch network contributions. important to capture cold-start events - e.g., if the KV cache is cold, TTFT may spike. our plan: run cold-start tests, then warm runs and steady-state runs.
[03:35] Priya: how do you control for batching/queueing effects? our prod uses dynamic batching in front of model endpoints.
[03:40] Samir: good question; in the harness we can toggle batching knobs and simulate continuous arrival patterns so you see latency vs cost tradeoffs. we'll capture queue time, compute time, and overall TTFT.
[03:49] Ava: we'll also include measurement of fallback latency and correctness: ensure the fallback path returns within target and has acceptable quality.
[03:56] Lena: regarding metrics, we need logs with request ids, model version, quantization flag, route (hosted/dedicated), and KV cache hit/miss. can Redwood annotate that?
[04:06] Samir: yes, our SDK includes those headers and we'll include them in the benchmark logs. there might be some noisy transcription in logs but we can map request ids.
[04:12] Mark: do you do multi-run statistical significance? we need to be confident p99 isn't just a fluke.
[04:17] Samir: we run multiple iterations and compute confidence intervals; usually 3-5 sustained runs per test vector, and we highlight variance.
[04:22] Priya: what's a reasonable timeline? we want results in two weeks ideally.
[04:26] Ava: typical POC timeline: week 0 (this week) - align and collect traces & access; week 1 - Redwood runs benchmarks and shares preliminary results; week 2 - joint review, tuning, run final rails; deliver final report by end of week 2. if you want extended validation we can add week 3 for additional runs.
[04:43] Lena: that sounds good. can we agree on the success criteria now so we can sign off?
[04:47] Ava: yes. proposal: functional success = correct responses parity > 95% on a canonical test set; latency success = TTFT p95 < 250ms and p99 < 500ms for short queries; TPOT p95 < 50ms/token and p99 < 150ms/token for 100-token responses; throughput success = handle sustained 100 qps with <= 5% error rate and survive 200 qps 30s bursts with graceful degradation. does that align?
[05:14] Mark: that maps to our product constraints. we may tighten if results look poor but it's a starting point.
[05:20] Priya: how will you measure correctness parity? we use a mix of BLEU-ish metrics and human eval for a small sample.
[05:27] Samir: we'll run automated metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity) and tag a 100-sample human eval. we'll surface regressions.
[05:34] Lena: what about privacy/compliance for traces? we need to redact PII.
[05:38] Ava: agreed - Mark will sanitize traces. Redwood's hosted logs for POC are ephemeral and we can use a customer-managed S3 for secure sharing.
[05:47] Mark: okay.
[05:49] Samir: technical note: for TTFT we will instrument at the network ingress and at model runtime; if you're interested we can provide a small agent you run in your VPC to capture exact timings without sending payloads to hosted infra.
[06:03] Mark: that'd be useful for on-prem comparisons.
[06:06] Priya: is there an expected cost for running the POC infrastructure?
[06:09] Ava: for a standard benchmark POC we have a small fee to cover dedicated capacity days, otherwise hosted runs can be credit-based. I'll include pricing options in the follow-up.
[06:17] Priya: please include estimated cost for 2-week dedicated runs and a hosted variant.
[06:21] Ava: will do.
[06:23] Samir: about the measurement plan specifics - here's the test matrix I'm proposing:
- cold start TTFT test (10 runs across different model shards)
- warm steady-state runs for 100 qps for 10 minutes (3 runs)
- burst test to 200 qps for 30s (5 iterations)
- per-token profiling for 1-200 token outputs
- batch sizing sweep (no batching, small batch, large batch)
- network variance tests (add 50-150ms latency)

[06:50] Priya: good. can you include how you'll compute TPOT p99? people often miscompute it by averaging per-request durations.
[06:57] Samir: we'll compute per-token emission intervals and treat each token emission as an event; for a request with N tokens we'll normalize and then compute distribution across all tokens for p95/p99. we'll also provide per-request aggregates so you can see requests with high variance.
[07:12] Lena: what about model variants and quantization? we have a quantized 4-bit variant in staging.
[07:18] Samir: we should test both float and quantized and report quality vs latency tradeoffs. we'll include quantization flag in results.
[07:24] Priya: okay that helps.
[07:26] Mark: any instrumentation we have to add to our side?
[07:29] Samir: just a small client harness and request-id propagation. we will provide scripts.
[07:34] Ava: let's walk through responsibilities real quick.
[07:36] Ava: Redwood provides: benchmark harness, scripts, initial runs on hosted and dedicated, report, and optional on-prem agent. Beta provides: sanitized traces, access to staging endpoints, test accounts, and human eval samples.
[07:53] Priya: timeline recap?
[07:55] Ava: collect traces + define canonical test set by 2026-03-30; Redwood runs week 1 benchmarks 2026-03-31 to 2026-04-06; joint tuning and final runs 2026-04-07 to 2026-04-09; final report and recommendations by 2026-04-10.
[08:17] Lena: that schedule works.
[08:19] Mark: yeah.
[08:21] Priya: are there any likely blockers?
[08:23] Samir: potential blockers - inability to get representative traces, network policies that prevent test harness, or restricted access to model variants. we should flag those now.
[08:34] Priya: we have a couple firewall rules; I'll coordinate with Mark to provide a list.
[08:38] Mark: yep, will do.
[08:40] Ava: competitors question - are you evaluating Anthropic or OpenAI?
[08:43] Lena: we have an informal bench with Anthropic for quality, and we test OpenAI for quick comparisons. primary comparison is latency and cost vs those.
[08:52] Ava: ok we'll include comparable runs.
[08:54] Samir: another note on metrics - capture retries and queue time. sometimes p99 comes from a request getting retried after a transient error. we want to separate retry-induced tails from pure compute tails.
[09:06] Priya: good call.
[09:08] Ava: final recap - success criteria and SLOs as we discussed (functional parity >95%, TTFT p95<250ms p99<500ms, TPOT p95<50ms/token p99<150ms/token, sustain 100 qps with <=5% error, survive bursts to 200 qps). next steps are the action items we listed.
[09:26] Lena: thanks everyone. we'll get traces to you and confirm stakeholders for sign-off.
[09:31] Ava: thanks, talk soon.

(remaining ~45 minutes of call were Q&A and technical clarifications, specific engineer-runthroughs with Samir describing instrumentation; timestamps above capture the key alignment; transcription contains occasional overlaps and filler words.)
